Human Growth & Development

Model Exam: Nov 9, Mon (10:00 AM – 12:00 PM) • University Exam: Nov 18, Wed (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM)
▼
Unit 1 ✓ Study Material Ready

Unit 1: Approaches to Human Development

1.1: Human development as a discipline from infancy to adulthood1.2: Concepts and Principles of development1.3: Developing Human- Stages (Prenatal development, Infancy, Childhood, Adolescence, Adulthood)1.4: Basic Understanding of Nature versus Nurture on Development1.5: Basic Understanding of Domains of Development of Physical, Sensory- perceptual, Cognitive, Socio-emotional, Language & communication, social relationship
Unit 2 ✓ Study Material Ready

Unit 2: Theoretical Perspectives on Human Development

2.1: Psychodynamic Theories: Basic Understanding of key concepts: Sigmund Freud’s Psychoanalytic theory and Erikson’s Psychosocial theory2.2: Cognitive Theories: Basic Understanding of key concepts: Piaget and Bruner2.3: Social Constructive theory: Basic Understanding of key concepts- Lev Vygotskey2.4: Humanistic Theory: Basic Understanding of key concepts: Abraham Maslow2.5: Ecological theory: Basic Understanding of key concepts: Bronfenbrenner
Unit 3

Unit 3: Prenatal and Early years (Zero -Eight years)

3.1: Prenatal development: Stages and influences on prenatal development3.2: Screening the newborn -APGAR Score, Reflexes and responses, neuro-perceptual development3.3: Basic Milestones and variations in Development3.4: Environmental factors influencing early childhood development3.5: Role of play in enhancing development
Unit 4

Unit 4: Early Adolescence (From nine years to eighteen years)

4.1: Emerging capabilities across domains of physical, social emotional4.2: Emerging capabilities across domains related to cognition-Meta Cognition and Creativity4.3: Issues related to puberty4.4: Gender and development4.5: Influence of the environment on the growing child
Unit 5

Unit 5: Transitions into Adulthood

5.1: Psychological well-being5.2: Formation of identity and self-concept5.3: Emerging roles and responsibilities5.4: Life Skills and Independent Living5.5: Career Choices
A2 60 Hours • 2 Credits • 50 Marks

Contemporary India and Education

Model Exam: Nov 9, Mon (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM) • University Exam: Nov 19, Thu (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM)
▼
Unit 1

Unit 1: Philosophical Foundations of Education

1.1: Education: Meaning and definition, nature and scope;1.2: Aims and Agencies of Education1.3: Schools of Philosophy: Idealism, Naturalism, Pragmatism, Existentialism and Humanism.1.4: Historical Perspectives of Indian Education: Gandhi, Tagore and Vivekananda.1.5: Classical Indian Philosophies: Vedanta Darshan, Sankya Darshan, Budhism and Jainism
Unit 2

Unit 2: Understanding Diversity

2.1: Diversity: Concept, Nature and Types2.2: Diversity in disability2.3: Diversity and learning: Diversity in classroom, Diversity in schooling (Inclusive Education as a right based model. Complementarity of Inclusive and Special Schools)2.4: Global Perspective: United Nations mandate on Disability, International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF 2001 by WHO)2.5: UN SDGs: Good Health and Wellbeing as a Sustainable Development Goal (UN SDG3), Quality Education as a Sustainable Development Goal (UN SDG4), Gender Equality as a Sustainable Development Goal (UN SDG5), Reduced Inequality as a Sustainable Development Goal (UN SDG10)
Unit 3

Unit 3: Commissions, Acts and Policies on Education in General and Children with Disabilities

3.1: National Commissions,: University Education Commission (1948-49), Secondary Education Commission (1952-53), Education Commission (1964-66);3.2: National Policy on Education (NPE 1968), National Policy of Education (NPE 1986 and POA1992), National Education Policy (NEP, 2020)3.3: National Curriculum Framework (NCF, 2005), National Curriculum Framework for Teacher Education (NCFTE, 2009), National Curriculum Framework for School Education (NCFSE, 2023)3.4: International Conventions and Policies: Salamanca Declaration and Framework, 1994; UNCRPD, 2006 (United Nations Committee on Right of Persons with Disabilities); MDG, 2015 (The Millennium Development Goals Report); INCHEON strategies (United Nations effort, Incheon Gan 2030); Biwako Millennium Framework.3.5: National Acts: RCI Act, 1992, PWD (Persons with Disability) Act, 1995, NT (National Trust) Act, 1999; The Right of Persons with Disability Act 2016.
Unit 4

Unit 4: Development in School Education and Equal Educational Opportunity

4.1: Constitutional Provisions: Reflecting on ideas of Equality, Liberty, Secularism, and Social Justice; Constitutional Provisions on Right to Education, Women Education, Education for the Weaker Section and Minorities, Education for the Diverse Need Sections.4.2: Meaning of equality, equity and equality, prevailing nature and forms of inequality, including dominant and minority groups and related issues; inequality in schooling: public-private schools, rural-urban schools, single teacher schools and other forms of inequalities such as regular and distance education systems.4.3: Right to Education, (RTE) Act 2009 &20124.4: Landmarks in Development of Education of Children with Disabilities: concept of disability in Surgeon Report(2005), Disability in Charter Act 1823, Central Advisory Board of Education (CABE 1923), Indian perspective on Disability (Divyang Jan)4.5: Programmes and Schemes: IEDC (1974, 1983) (Integrated Education for the Disabled Children), Samarga Shiksha AbhiyanSSA (2000, 2011) (Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan), RMSA, 2009 (Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan), IEDSS, 2009 (Inclusive Education of the Disabled at the Secondary Stage)
Unit 5

Unit 5: Challenges in Education and Professional Development of Teachers

5.1: Challenges of education across different levels from foundational to secondary stage5.2: Professional Development of Teachers: In-service Teacher Education and Professional Development of Teachers (NEP 2020).5.3: Professional Ethics of the Teachers and Its Importance, Professional Identity of Teachers, Teacher as a Researcher, Teacher as a Facilitator5.4: Strategies for addressing the Issues of Professional Development of Teachers.5.5: Role of NCERT, SCERT and NCTE in professional development
B1 60 Hours • 2 Credits • 50 Marks

Introduction to Disabilities

Model Exam: Nov 10, Tue (10:00 AM – 12:00 PM) • University Exam: Nov 20, Fri (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM)
▼
Unit I ✓ Study Material Ready

Unit I: Basics of disability

1.1: Exceptionality: Concept, Types, Strengths and Characteristics1.2: Diversity, Difficulty, Delay & Disability in learners1.3: Myths and realities about disabilities. 2e- Twice exceptionality1.4: 21 Specified disabilities in RPwD (2016) and their educational implications1.5: International Classification of Functioning (ICF) framework of WHO; inaccessible environments as a source of barriers for learners with disabilities
Unit 2 ✓ Study Material Ready

Unit 2: Significant provisions for empowerment of learners with disabilities in RPWD Act (2016)

2.1: Respect for difference and acceptance of persons with disabilities as part of human diversity2.2: Benchmark disabilities & high support needs2.3: Reasonable accommodations, equality and equity2.4: Accessibility & barrier free environment for different disabilities2.5: Effective participation and inclusion
Unit 3

Unit 3: Characteristics, incidence, prevalence, types, and needs of persons with;

3.1: Locomotor disabilities and Muscular Dystrophy3.2: Cerebral Palsy and other neurological conditions3.3: Blindness and Low vision3.4: Hearing impairment3.5: Speech and language disabilities
Unit 4

Unit 4: Characteristics, incidence, prevalence, types, and needs of persons with;

4.1: Intellectual Disability4.2: Autism Spectrum Disorder4.3: Specific Learning Disabilities4.4: Multiple Disability and Deafblindness4.5: Mental Illness
Unit 5

Unit 5: Characteristics, incidence, prevalence, types, and needs of persons with; (Other Disabilities in RPwD Act and Sensitivity issues)

5.1: Blood Disorders: Thalassemia, Sickle Cell Disease & Haemophilia5.2: Chronic Neurological Conditions: Parkinson’s Disease & Multiple Sclerosis5.3: Other Specified Disabilities: Acid Attack victims, Leprosy Cured Persons & Dwarfism5.4: Use of respectable and ‘person first’ language and preserve identity & Avoid labeling except for certification purposes5.5: Understand intersectionality of disability & Eliminate stereotypes
C1 60 Hours • 2 Credits • 50 Marks

Identification of Disability and Assessment of Needs

Model Exam: Nov 10, Tue (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM) • University Exam: Nov 23, Mon (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM)
▼
Unit 1

Unit 1: Early Identification of Hearing Loss: Need and Strategies

1.1 Need for and importance of early identification of hearing loss.1.2 Auditory, speech and language milestones in typical children (0-2 years).1.3 Use of checklists and behavioral observation in early identification of hearing loss by school teachers (congenital & acquired).1.4 Team members involved in hearing screening and their role.1.5 Referral of children based on signs and symptoms of hearing loss.
Unit 2

Unit 2: Audiological Assessment

2.1 Orientation: Sound, Physical and psychological parameters/attributes.2.2 Assessment & methods of assessment: Subjective (informal and formal hearing tests) & Objective tests; Orientation to these tests and their importance.2.3 Audiometer: Block diagram, parts & use.2.4 Audiogram: Concept of aided and unaided audiograms, interpretation of audiogram and its implications in assessing the educational needs of children with hearing loss.2.5 Concept of speech spectrum and its applications.
Unit 3

Unit 3: Assessment of Communication & Language

3.1 Communication: Meaning and types.3.2 Language: concepts, types (verbal and manual) and structure.3.3 Receptive and expressive verbal language and need for its assessment.3.4 Impact of various environmental factors such as parental hearing status, family involvement on communication and language.3.5 Impact of various types, degrees and onset of hearing loss on communication and language.
Unit 4

Unit 4: Assessment of Speech

4.1 Speech: definition, prerequisites for the production of speech.4.2 Basics of respiration, articulation and phonation (active and passive articulators)4.3 Segmental, non-segmental and Supra-segmental aspects of speech and its assessment.4.4 Speech intelligibility: Meaning and assessment.4.5 Description and classification (vowels and consonants) of speech sounds and orientation to speech acoustics
Unit 5

Unit 5: Educational Assessment and Indian sign language

5.1 Educational assessment: Concept and scope5.2 Factors affecting educational performance: individual, family and environment.5.3 ISL: prerequisites, processes and need for assessment.5.4 Basics of ISL Parameters and their role in early sign language acquisition. Development of ISL through the ages.5.5 Assessment of various components of ISL (hand-shape, palm orientation, position of the hands, movement of the hands and non-hand components such as the use of the face, facial expressions, or body posture).
C2 60 Hours • 2 Credits • 50 Marks

Curriculum Development, Adaptation and Evaluation

Model Exam: Nov 11, Wed (10:00 AM – 12:00 PM) • University Exam: Nov 24, Tue (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM)
▼
Unit 1

Unit 1: Curriculum and Its Designing

1.1. Curriculum - Concept, Principles, Types and Models.1.2. Curriculum designing, concept and principles.1.3. Approaches and steps for curriculum designing.1.4. Curricular needs of children with hearing impairment in scholastic areas.1.5. Curricular needs of children with hearing impairment in non-scholastic areas.
Unit 2

Unit 2: Developing Literacy skills: Reading

2.1. Reading: Meaning and Pre-requisites of reading.2.2. Types and models of developing reading skills.2.3. Approaches and strategies to develop reading skills (Bilingual strategies).2.4. Assessment of reading skills at different levels.2.5. Challenges and remedial strategies.
Unit 3

Unit 3: Developing Literacy Skills: Writing

3.1. Meaning and pre-requisites of Writing.3.2. Components and types of writing.3.3. Steps and strategies in developing writing (Bilingual strategies).3.4. Assessment of written language at different levels.3.5. Challenges and remedial strategies.
Unit 4

Unit 4: Curricular Adaptation

4.1. Curricular Adaptation- Meaning and principles.4.2. Types of adaptation and process.4.3. Need assessment and decision making for adaptation.4.4. Adapting Curriculum- Content, teaching-learning material, and instruction.4.5. Adaptation and accommodations in student’s evaluation and examinations.
Unit 5

Unit 5: Curricular Evaluation

5.1. Concept and need for curricular evaluation.5.2. Factors associated with curricular evaluation (Learner, Content, Instructor and Resources).5.3. Areas of curricular evaluation: Context, Input, Process and Product.5.4. Methods and tools for curricular evaluation.5.5. Challenges in curricular evaluation.
C3 60 Hours • 2 Credits • 50 Marks

Intervention and Teaching Strategies

Model Exam: Nov 11, Wed (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM) • University Exam: Nov 25, Wed (02:00 PM – 04:00 PM)
▼
Unit 1

Unit 1: Need & Strategies for Early Intervention of Hearing Loss

1.1 Parent-infant programmes for children with HI: Overview, need, requirements and plan of action.1.2 Pre-school training programmes: Overview, need, requirements and plan of action.1.3 Individual speech-language therapy programs: Overview, need, requirements and plan of action.1.4 Impact of early intervention on school outcomes.1.5 Intervention of late identified children with hearing impairment: Challenges & strategies.
Unit 2

Unit 2: Auditory Learning, Speechreading

2.1 Auditory training: Importance, stages, types, factors affecting auditory training2.2 Auditory Verbal Therapy: Principles, pre-requisites, strategies2.3 Similarities and difference between auditory training and AVT2.4 Speech reading: Need, methods, factors affecting speech reading2.5 Role of teacher in Auditory training, AVT and Speech reading
Unit 3

Unit 3: Speech, communication and Language Teaching Strategies

3.1 Speech intervention strategies –Approaches (Auditory Global approach, Multisensory syllable unit approach, ling's approach) Uni sensory and multi sensory approach.3.2 Teaching speech to CwHI-Formulation of lesson plan and activities for speech teaching, correction, strategies for production of speech (modelling, shaping)3.3 Individual and group speech teaching and their strengths and limitations3.4 Methods of teaching language: Natural, Structural and Combined3.5 Techniques of teaching language
Unit 4

Unit 4: Bilingual Teaching Strategies for Deaf Children

4.1 Principles of developing language and early language acquisition.4.2 Methods of teaching language: Natural, Structural and Combined.4.3 Techniques of teaching language.4.4 Maxims of teaching language.4.5 Tuning the environment (home and school) for facilitating language and communication.
Unit 5

Unit 5: Educational Intervention Strategies

5.1 Educational Intervention: Concept, Need & Areas (curricular & co-curricular)5.2 Types of educational intervention (group, individual, developmental, remedial).5.3 Principles and practices in early educational intervention: Family centred, contextualized (natural & inclusive environment) & integrated (collaborative) support and services.5.4 Partnership of various professionals & agencies in educational intervention.5.5 Child & Family Outcomes of Early Educational Intervention.
Practicum 240 Hours • 8 Credits • 200 Marks

Practicum: Area E1 (HI) & Area E2 (HI)

Model Exam: Internal Practical Submission • University Exam: Semester 1 Practical Evaluation
▼
Area E1 (HI)

Area E1 (HI): Visits & Writing Reports

1. Visits to special schools/ Deaf Associations/Training Centres which use Educational Bilingualism, Total Communication, Oral-aural approach2. Visit to speech and hearing center/clinic
Area E2 (HI)

Area E2 (HI): Micro Teaching & Classroom Observation at Different Levels and of Different Subjects

1. Practicing and performing Micro teaching skills and link practice.2. Classroom teaching observation at different levels and of different subjects using : Educational Bilingualism, Total Communication, Oral-aural approach
